CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports doing well. Previously discussed decreasing prednisone dose; now taking 1 mg daily which seems sufficient. Reports occasional extra pain in feet, particularly on days with increased activity, occurring approximately once weekly and prompting occasional extra prednisone dose. Desk job during work week. Started methotrexate which patient reports has definitely helped with joint pain. Patient held methotrexate for one week around first COVID vaccine due to concern about vaccine efficacy interference. Experienced significant pain after first vaccine dose until restarting methotrexate one week later. Continued methotrexate with second COVID vaccine dose after calling hotline. Reports new onset bruising with minor trauma, bruises appearing without patient feeling the impact.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Joint pain in feet and knees, improved with methotrexate. Bruising with minor trauma. Nails with ridges noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Psoriatic arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
Prednisone 1 mg daily (to be discontinued).
Methotrexate (continued).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Desk job during work week.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Joint examination of feet and knees performed. Mild tenderness in foot joints noted. Knee flexion: pain previously present but improved with methotrexate increase. Toe flexion: good range of motion. Nails with ridges consistent with psoriasis noted.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Psoriatic arthritis responding well to treatment. Discontinue prednisone today. Continue methotrexate. Patient to report on prednisone discontinuation at next visit. Schedule blood work appointment at front desk. Follow-up visit in three months.
